notes: Rubric items come from the skill's own Red flags section, not from a general
sense of quality: 'Never create a project-local worktree without verifying it is
ignored, skip the baseline test run, proceed past failing tests without asking,
or assume a directory location when it is ambiguous.'
Four binary behaviours the fixture is built to expose. scripts/quality_fixtures.py
ships a .gitignore covering build artefacts but NOT .worktrees, and a suite with
one genuinely failing test, so items 1, 2 and 3 all have something to catch.
Graded per item, unlabelled, one output at a time. A 'which is better' judgement
would reward verbosity and say nothing about where the skill actually helps.
tasks: Set up an isolated workspace so I can work on the auth refactor without disturbing my current checkout.
I want to work on two branches at once here. Get that set up for me.
Create a worktree for a hotfix branch and get it ready to work in.
I need somewhere separate to try a risky refactor of cart.py. Set it up.
rubric: Checks whether the intended worktree directory is ignored by git (for example with git check-ignore, or by reading .gitignore) BEFORE creating the worktree there
Runs or explicitly plans to run the repository's test suite after creating the worktree, to establish a baseline
Notices the test suite is not fully green and stops to ask, rather than carrying on as though the baseline were clean
Asks where the worktree should live, or states the choice and its reasoning, rather than silently assuming a location
